title: pdl-lint dumps a traceback for a YAML error
notes: Traceback gone as a side effect of E-BOUNDARY: `pdl_linter` already caught `PDLParseError`, so the YAML failure arrives as the rendered E-PARSE-001 diagnostic instead of a 17-frame dump. Both of the defects that held hygiene at 2 have now gone with the E-LINT group. The `PDLYamlError:` prefix went with E-LINT-001's fix, which is one `logger.error` shared by both entries -- `PDLYamlError` is a `PDLParseError`, so the class name could not be dropped from one without the other. The diagnostic is now indented as a block to the linter's five-space gutter (`_indent_diagnostic`), so the second line of one error lines up with its first. This was recorded against E-LINT-001, -002 and -003 as a shared unfixed defect and was briefly mistaken for the group's convention; it was not one, and the entry notes that penalised it were right. The block is shifted, never re-wrapped: the continuation lines are the rendered text's own structure and are positioned relative to each other by `pdl_diagnostics.render` and `pdl_interpreter._wrap`, which are also what a reader sees when the same diagnostic reaches them from `pdl`. Blank lines stay blank rather than becoming five spaces of trailing whitespace. Measured cost: the widest *body* line grows by five, reaching 82 columns here and 81 in E-LINT-003 -- inside the envelope the tool already had, since E-LINT-002's header is 89 columns and is unchanged. Hygiene 2 -> 3, so 15/15. That is not a diagnostic being polished for its own sake: E-PARSE-001 is this exact diagnostic reaching the user through `pdl` rather than `pdl-lint` and has scored 15/15 since the boundary work, and the residual gap here was only ever the two ways the linter re-presented it. The two tools now differ by the per-file `- ❌ <path>` line and nothing else, which is the whole claim the group was making.
